articleTitle: Data-Driven Based Preconditioning for One-Bit MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology is a keystone for a wide range of wireless communications applications. Therefore, great efforts have been made to design efficient and high-performance MIMO detection algorithms. Current state-of-the-art methods are model-based algorithms such as the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). However, these methods are limited to the ill-conditioned nature of the channel matrix producing subpar convergence and recovery performance. To address this issue, preconditioning methods employ a matrix (denoted as preconditioning matrix) in the algorithm iterations to mitigate the instabilities caused by the ill-conditioned channel matrix. Here, we present a method to design the preconditioning matrix in a data-driven manner. The method is inspired by the knowledge distillation theory of neural networks. Specifically, we use a well-conditioned (virtual) channel matrix, that has a high MIMO detection performance, as guidance to optimize the preconditioning matrix. Intuitively, the preconditioning matrix is designed such that the estimated signal via the preconditioned algorithm with the ill-conditioned channel matrix is similar to the one obtained with the well-conditioned channel matrix. We validate the method using an ADMM algorithm, showing a significant detection improvement using the proposed preconditioning method. Additionally, we show that the proposed guidance method for designing the preconditioning matrix allows better detection than using a supervised loss function.

articleTitle: Point Spread Function Estimation Using Principal Component Analysis for a Double Diffractive Optical Element System
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: Spectral image (SI) acquisition relies on optical systems implementation; some systems as the shift-variant, require a calibration process where the point spread function (PSF) is acquired at each spatial point. Acquiring the complete PSF of an optical system is a complex and time-consuming process as it requires several snapshots, each one with a high acquisition time. For these reasons, this paper proposes a method to obtain an approximation of the PSF for a double diffractive optical element (DOE) system by capturing a set of calibration patterns designed using principal component analysis (PCA). Simulation results showed that by using 84% fewer snapshots, it is possible to obtain a PSF with an average peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 40 dB and an average structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 90%. Implementation results showed an average PSNR of 40 dB and an average SSIM of 71% with 97.7% fewer snapshots.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Pulmonary Arterial Segmentation in Computed Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: Pulmonary Embolism (PE) is a life-threatening condition in which a blood clot blocks an artery in the lungs. It remains one of the most challenging conditions to diagnose and treat in the emergency department. Early detection and timely treatment are critical to improving patient outcomes. In this work, we seek to develop and implement an algorithm for automated pulmonary artery segmentation as a crucial step toward PE identification. We had access to a database of 130 CT volumes with refined labeling of pulmonary arteries. We propose the implementation of an architecture called ResD-Unet, based on the Unet network, complemented with residual blocks and interconnected convolution layers. The segmentation quality was measured using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC). The proposed architecture yielded a DSC of 0.76. Although the results obtained are modest, they represent a first step towards solving the problem and underline the feasibility and potential for future improvements of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Visual and Inertial Odometry Based on Sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: Given conventional procedures of visual odometry based on stereo vision could have problems with detection if an environmental object is not in a fixed location. It is important to consider the possibility of adding more sensors. In this case, an IMU presents an additional information source. For this reason, using sensor fusion is important, it is a way to improve methods for pose estimation. This research was focused on developing a Visual Odometry (VO) method based on stereovision and Inertial Odometry (IO) by applying sensor fusion. The main goal of this method was to improve the possibilities of robot autonomous navigation. The pose estimation using this methods has been planned as an option for not losing accuracy with moving objects or light noise that affect the visual odometry. This project has been tested in a mobile platform, and designed for future drone applications.

articleTitle: Detecting False Arrhythmias Alarms in the ICU Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: In the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), false arrhythmia alarms become a constant disturbance that generates stress for both medical staff and patients. The high rate of these reports, coupled with the inability of monitoring systems to accurately discern between normal cardiac signals and arrhythmias, compromises the quality of care and puts patients' health at risk. The aim of this research was to identify false alarms using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained with data from the PhysioNet Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2015 database. In addition, we explored the effectiveness of data augmentation techniques in the training of the model; the performance evaluation metrics used included true positive rate (TPR), true negative rate (TNR), F1 score, area under the curve (AUC), and final score of the PhysioNet Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2015. The results suggest that the model achieved a Physionet score of 65.24. Additionally, they reveal that data augmentation techniques did not have a significant impact on false alarm identification.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstruction of Cultural Heritage Pieces Using Depth Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: Depth sensors are a very useful technology that in recent years has had a rapid development making them more portable and easier to use for archaeological studies and heritage preservation. These technologies are cheap (economically and computationally), and easy to operate, they can be moved to sites and make reconstructions in indoors and outdoors. This research laid on the opportunity of having access to archaeology pieces to improve the categorisation and the conservation of those archaeological findings without extracting them from their sites. Different depth sensors were evaluated by comparing software and open-source techniques for the reconstruction of small and medium-sized heritage, making a contrast in qualitative and quantitative level. The main goal of this study is to evaluate different methods of 3D object reconstruction with different RGB-D and stereovision devices, achieving the configuration with best performance for 3D reconstruction of small pieces.

articleTitle: Transforming Agriculture: Drones Enhancing Livestock Management with AI Precision
publicationTitle: 2024 XXIV Symposium of Image, Signal Processing, and Artificial Vision (STSIVA)
abstract: In Colombia, livestock farming represents an important source of income, contributing 27% to agricultural Gross Domestic Product. However, this activity faces various challenges to ensure its proper development, such as cattle theft, known as rustling. This problem is what we seek to address with this project, which proposes a counting and monitoring system through aerial surveillance of livestock. Such results are achieved using images captured by a drone and further processed by an artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm. Remarkably, a key aspect of the project is the establishment of a database, collecting 1546 aerial images of livestock in 4 locations in Santander and Boyacá, Colombia. After rigorous labeling of the images, we proceeded to train the YoloV8m model. With the implementation of this model, we achieved an accuracy of 95.1%, precision of 96.1%, a sensitivity of 98.9%, and F1 metric of 97.47%. These results validate the model's ability to detect cows.
